source_receipts.result: The Senate rejected the House-passed resolution 48–51. Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul voted for it.

In an Axios interview, the retiring Republican senator said the Pentagon had shared too little about its discussions with the White House. She said House Democrats might revisit Pete Hegseth’s impeachment in January.
Axios reports that Gill, who backed Jim Jordan for party leader, and Fallon, who backed Steve Scalise, want the ranking Republican post. Republican whip Tom Emmer publicly backs Gill.

AP reports that the department asked the appeals court to vacate the lower court ruling and dismiss the case as moot after Mary Peltola won an outright majority in unofficial returns. Trump had pressed for the suit before the result.

The solicitor general told the Supreme Court that the appeals court kept the lower court’s order on hold until seven days after the appeals court publishes judgment. The government withdrew its emergency Supreme Court request on November 19.
The Senate passed amended H.R. 2347 by 62–33. AP reports the proposal would speed federal reviews and require data centers to cover power costs. The House previously passed a different version.

Axios reports that Frey vetoed the ordinance after it passed 7–6. He argued that the council’s restrictions would effectively prevent development. The council was due to consider an override November 20.
Treasury extended permission to negotiate and sign contingent contracts through December 19. A buyer still needs separate Treasury approval to complete a sale.

The Senate rejected the House-passed Iran withdrawal resolution 48–51. Rand Paul, Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski backed it. The vote leaves Trump free to continue the current operation. A new strike order or response to Gulf mediators remains unverified.

dated_assumptions.assumption: House response to Senate permitting bill
dated_assumptions.reason: Senate passage is verified. House agreement and enactment remain open.

major_developments.finding: Senate rejects resolution to withdraw U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran
major_developments.reason: Trump retains immediate military discretion. Paul can point to a recorded vote for withdrawal when speaking to Republican opponents of the war.

major_developments.finding: Senator Joni Ernst criticizes Pentagon disclosures about the Iran war
major_developments.reason: Criticism from a Republican on the Armed Services Committee makes it harder for Hegseth to dismiss demands for information as partisan. Ernst gave no trial commitment in the published account.

major_developments.finding: Brandon Gill and Pat Fallon seek the top Republican seat on House Oversight
major_developments.reason: The post would give its holder a platform to defend Trump during Democratic inquiries. Republican committee recommendations and the conference vote still lie ahead.

major_developments.finding: Justice Department asks appeals court to end its challenge to Alaska’s Senate result
major_developments.reason: Peltola can point to a clear lead as she calls for moving on. The filing reduces the immediate threat to certification. The court disposition, certification and disputed campaign allegations remain separate questions.

major_developments.finding: Appeals court extends the pause on restoring temporary protection for Venezuelans
major_developments.reason: The administration can continue to enforce the termination while the pause lasts. The appeals court still has to decide the case.

major_developments.finding: Senate passes bill to speed energy permits and require data centers to cover power costs
major_developments.reason: The vote shows bipartisan support for changing permitting rules. The House still has to act before the Senate proposal can become law.

major_developments.finding: Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey vetoes data-center zoning restrictions
major_developments.reason: The veto gives supporters of downtown development leverage over siting rules. An override would require nine votes. The outcome was unverified at review time.

major_developments.finding: Treasury extends the deadline for talks on selling Lukoil’s international business
major_developments.reason: Treasury gives bidders more time while retaining control over whether a sale can close and under what conditions.

major_developments.finding: Republican primary surveys disagree on whether Rubio or Vance leads
major_developments.reason: Rubio has a credible claim to voter interest alongside his support inside the administration. Differences in samples and candidate lists limit conclusions about who leads nationally. Neither survey measures organizing or delegate commitments.

challenges.alternative: A Republican senator’s public criticism implies support for conviction.
challenges.finding: Ernst criticized disclosures and is retiring. She gave no trial commitment in published coverage.
challenges.consequence: Record broader pressure for records and hold the removal estimates.

challenges.alternative: A single post-election survey establishes the national primary leader.
challenges.finding: Emerson found Rubio ahead of Vance in both its named and open-ended questions. Echelon found Vance ahead with a different list. Both have a plausible voter base, while the polling split leaves their relative strength unsettled.
challenges.consequence: Recognize Rubio’s voter support and test persistence in the weekly review.

assessment_audit.summary_reason: The Senate votes, court stay, polling and oversight pressure change the current picture.
